title: A Late-Night Call About Gossip at the Office
script: Dinda: [worried] Ilham, sorry for calling so late. I just need to talk to someone about work today.
Ilham: [calmly] No problem at all. What happened over there?
Dinda: My coworker Wulan made a huge mistake on our project, and now I really want to tell everyone about it.
Ilham: Why do you want to tell everyone specifically, do you think?
Dinda: [frustrated] I don't know, maybe because I'm frustrated, or maybe because part of me wants people to know it wasn't my fault.
Ilham: That's an honest answer. But would talking about her mistake actually fix anything for the project?
Dinda: No, probably not. It would just make her look bad in front of everyone at the office.
Ilham: I remember something my grandmother used to say, before you speak about someone, imagine they're standing right behind you.
Dinda: [reflective] That's actually a strong image. I definitely wouldn't say those things with Wulan standing there listening.
Ilham: Exactly. It's easy to talk about people when they can't hear us, but much harder when we imagine them present.
Dinda: I already told two people about it this afternoon, actually, before I even thought carefully about any of this.
Ilham: That happens to all of us sometimes. What matters now is what you decide to do next.
Dinda: [regretfully] Maybe I should talk to Wulan directly instead, about fixing the mistake, rather than talking about her to others.
Ilham: That sounds much wiser. And maybe a quiet word to the two coworkers, asking them to let it stay between you all.
Dinda: Okay. Tomorrow morning, I'll talk to Wulan first, calmly, before this spreads any further around the office.
Ilham: Good. Our careless words can cause a lot of trouble, I honestly think.
Dinda: I never really thought carefully about that before tonight, if I'm being honest.
Ilham: Most people don't, until a story travels somewhere it never should have gone in the first place.
Dinda: [grateful] Thank you for listening, and for not just agreeing with me out of politeness.
Ilham: That's what old friends are for, Dinda. Call me tomorrow and tell me how it goes with Wulan.
